At Traton, I develop embedded software for the next generation of electric and hybrid trucks and buses, supporting the shift to sustainable transport.
Within the Thermal Management Systems team at Scania, I design and implement software that ensures the safe, reliable, and energy-efficient operation of vehicle and battery systems.
We take system ownership of core thermal functionalities and collaborate closely with cross-functional teams across Traton R&D to align strategies and harmonize software platforms.
Our work spans the full embedded lifecycle and includes:
Thermal strategies for batteries, power electronics, and cabin systems
Supervision, control and coordination of auxiliaries (fans, valves, pumps, compressors)
Charger integration and thermal coordination
SOC/SOH-optimized thermal control strategies
We follow a model-based development approach using Matlab/Simulink and embedded C, enabling early validation and smooth integration into production ECUs.
Our development process is fully aligned with ISO 26262 (ASIL B) and A-SPICE standards, incorporating diagnostics, fault handling, and fallback strategies for robust field operation.
CI/CD pipelines in GitLab support continuous integration and rapid iteration with high software quality, avoiding integration issues before reaching HIL or vehicle testing.
Working in a SAFe agile environment, our team reduces development cycles from months to weeks, accelerating the deployment of software solutions across Traton’s global electric vehicle platforms.

entries.title: Modular Design and Integration of In-Cycle Closed-Loop Combustion Controllers for a Wide-Range of Operating Conditions
entries.description: Investigated the modular design and integration of in-cycle closed-loop combustion controllers for seamless operation across various conditions. Tested on a Scania D13 engine, confirming improved controllability and reduced steady-state RMSE of controlled parameters with smoother transitions.
impact_metrics: Reduced steady-state RMSE of controlled parameters

entries.title: Stochastic Set-Point Optimization for In-Cycle Closed-Loop Combustion Control Operation
entries.description: Developed a novel approach for constrained indicated efficiency optimization of set-point references for in-cycle closed-loop combustion regulators. By including the effect of controlled variables on combustion dispersion and solving the stochastic optimization problem, indicated efficiency can be increased by up to +1.8%unit at low loads and +0.6%unit at medium loads compared to open-loop operation. The greatest advantage was achieved by regulating CA50 under demanding maximum pressure rise rate constraints. Considering pilot misfire risk, indicated efficiency can be increased additionally by +0.3%unit.
impact_metrics: Increased indicated efficiency by up to +1.8%unit at low loads
Increased indicated efficiency by up to +0.6%unit at medium loads
Increased indicated efficiency by an additional +0.3%unit by considering pilot misfire risk

entries.title: In-Cycle Closed-Loop Combustion Control for Pilot Misfire Compensation
entries.description: Investigated how in-cycle closed-loop combustion control techniques can reduce the effects of pilot misfire events by detecting and counteracting them in-cycle. Explored two injection strategies: control of the main injection and an additional second pilot injection.

entries.title: Multi-Cylinder Adaptation of In-Cycle Predictive Combustion Models
entries.description: Studied the adaptation of predictive combustion models for in-cycle closed-loop combustion control of multi-cylinder engines, enabling closer operation to the optimal point despite variations and disturbances.

entries.title: Predictive In-Cycle Closed-Loop Combustion Control with Pilot-Main Injections
entries.description: Utilized predictive in-cycle closed-loop combustion control to reduce stochastic cyclic variations in diesel combustion. Implemented on a Scania D13 engine, the approach reduced error dispersion (measured by 95% confidence interval) by 25% to 75% for all controlled parameters. On-line adaptation made controllers robust against model uncertainties and fuel types.
impact_metrics: Reduced error dispersion by 25% to 75% for all controlled parameters
Controllers are robust against model uncertainties and fuel types

entries.title: Bayesian Method for Fuel Mass Estimation of Short Pilot Injections based on its Misfire Probability
entries.description: Proposed and analyzed a Bayesian method for fuel mass estimation of short pilot diesel injections, particularly in regions with low signal-to-noise ratio. Experimental results on a Scania D13 Diesel engine confirmed a 60% reduction in estimation error (from 0.66mg to 0.27mg standard deviation) in the transition region from full misfire to full combustion.
impact_metrics: 60% reduction in estimation error (from 0.66mg to 0.27mg standard deviation)

entries.title: Cylinder Pressure Based Method for In-Cycle Pilot Misfire Detection
entries.description: Developed and evaluated in-cycle algorithms for pilot misfire detection based on in-cylinder pressure measurements. Compared different approaches including constant threshold, direct misfire probability, posterior misfire probability, adaptive threshold update, adaptation of predictive stochastic models, and sensor fusion for increased detection performance.

entries.title: In-Cycle Closed-Loop Combustion Control for Maximum Indicated Efficiency
entries.description: Proposed an in-cycle closed-loop combustion controller using a pilot-main injection scheme. Implemented on a Scania D13 Diesel engine, the controller adjusted main SOI and duration to achieve Maximum Reachable Indicated Efficiency (MRE). Results showed improved indicated efficiency, though linear controller application was limited by non-linear system behavior dependent on fuel type.

entries.title: In-Cycle Closed-Loop Combustion Controllability with Pilot-Main Injections
entries.description: Investigated the in-cycle closed-loop combustion controllability achieved by a pilot-main fuel injection scheme, studied through the maximum reachable indicated thermal efficiency (MRE).

entries.title: Internal Combustion Engine Cylinder Volume Trace Deviation
entries.description: Investigated the validity of the nominal cylinder volume assumption in heavy-duty engines, considering production variations, static distortion, and dynamic deformation. Developed a virtual sensor (VS) that reduced cylinder volume error from static distortion and dynamic deformation to below 0.4%.
impact_metrics: Reduced cylinder volume error to below 0.4%

entries.title: Cylinder Pressure Based Virtual Sensor for In-Cycle Pilot Mass Estimation
entries.description: Proposed a virtual sensor for in-cycle pilot mass estimation, providing early estimation even with incomplete combustion. The accuracy of pilot mass estimation was improved from an induced initial bias error of ±3 mg/st to a final error of ±0.1 mg/st, with a precision of ±0.45 mg/st. The method is robust against changing operating conditions and most input measurement errors and parameter bias.
impact_metrics: Improved pilot mass estimation accuracy from ±3 mg/st to ±0.1 mg/st
Robust against changing operating conditions and most input measurement errors and parameter bias

entries.title: Influence of small Pilot on Main Injection in a Heavy Duty Diesel Engine
entries.description: Investigated factors influencing the effect of pilot-injection on main-injection combustion in a heavy-duty diesel engine using heat release analysis. Identified four interaction modes between pilot and main injection based on the phase of pilot combustion at the start of main injection.

entries.title: FPGA Implementation of In-Cycle Closed-Loop Combustion Control Methods
entries.description: Investigated FPGA resources for implementing in-cycle closed-loop combustion control algorithms, comparing different methods for cylinder volume computation, heat capacity ratio, and virtual sensors for misfire detection and fuel mass estimation. Quantified hardware requirements to guide FPGA selection and evaluate system cost versus efficiency gains.

entries.title: Indicated efficiency optimization by in-cycle closed-loop combustion control of diesel engines
entries.description: Revised the design process for closed-loop combustion control based on in-cycle feedback, including methods for observers, detectors, and virtual sensors. The in-cycle controller increased indicated efficiency by +0.42%unit compared to open-loop operation. Indirect optimization reduced cyclic dispersion of pilot SOC (down to ±0.4CAD), pilot burnt mass (down to ±0.6 mg), main SOC (down to ±0.3CAD), and IMEP (down to ±0.2 bar). Pilot misfire detection compensated CA50 shift from +2.6CAD to +0.5CAD. Set-point optimization increased indicated efficiency by +0.6%unit under hardware and emission constraints.
impact_metrics: Reduced cyclic dispersion of pilot SOC to ±0.4CAD
Reduced cyclic dispersion of pilot burnt mass to ±0.6 mg
Reduced cyclic dispersion of main SOC to ±0.3CAD
Reduced cyclic dispersion of IMEP to ±0.2 bar
Increased indicated efficiency by +0.6%unit under constraints

entries.title: Investigation of small Pilot Combustion in a Heavy Duty Diesel Engine
entries.description: Investigated factors influencing pilot-injection combustion in a heavy-duty diesel engine using heat release analysis. Found that cycle-to-cycle and cylinder-to-cylinder variations influence pilot autoignition and heat release. Rail pressure and injected pilot mass affect variance depending on chamber conditions. Combustion modes were found to be a function of injected mass and rail pressure.

research_domains.name: Predictive Models for In-Cycle Combustion Control
evidence_sentences: To overcome the delay of the feedback signal and the control action, accurate predictive models are required for an effective in-cycle combustion control.

entries.title: Investigation of Small Pilot Combustion in a Heavy-Duty Diesel Engine
entries.summary: This paper investigates the factors influencing pilot-injection combustion in a heavy-duty diesel engine using heat release analysis. It studies combinations of pilot-injection parameters (start of injection, mass, pilot-main separation, rail pressure) under various operating conditions and combustion phases. The study also addresses improved injected fuel-mass accuracy by using reference data from a spray rig. Results indicate that cycle-to-cycle and cylinder-to-cylinder variations affect pilot autoignition and heat release. Rail pressure and injected pilot mass influence variance based on chamber conditions. entries.summary: This paper investigates the in-cycle closed-loop combustion controllability achieved by a pilot-main fuel injection scheme. The controllability is studied by means of the maximum reachable indicated efficiency (MRE). A combustion model is used for heat release optimization, simulating disturbances in the pilot combustion by modifying pilot model parameters. The MRE is obtained by optimizing heat release under constant load, with a disturbed pilot injection and adjusted main start of injection (SOI) and duration. The results show that pilot mass disturbances are the most influential factor on indicated efficiency, explaining 79% of its variability. Variances in the start of vaporization and start of combustion were also significant, depending on their interaction with pilot mass. Pilot combustion disturbances reduced net indicated efficiency by up to -0.8% units compared to the nominal maximum. Adjusting the main SOI improved indicated efficiency in 86% of cases by an average of +0.2% units, with a maximum improvement of +0.7% units for larger pilot masses, longer ignition delay, and increased combustion efficiency. Pilot injection is observable 1 CAD after its start of combustion, limiting main SOI controllability. In 13.8% of cases, the main SOI was uncontrollable. When constrained to the controllable window, the reduction in indicated efficiency was negligible.

entries.summary: This paper investigates the use of predictive in-cycle closed-loop combustion control to mitigate stochastic cyclic variations in diesel combustion. It utilizes pilot and main injection start of combustion, burned pilot mass, and engine load as set-point references. These metrics are predicted in-cycle using calibrated models based on cylinder state estimations from in-cylinder pressure measurements. The approach employs four individual controllers to minimize set-point errors by regulating pilot-main injection timing and duration. Implemented on an FPGA and tested in a Scania D13 engine, the controllers demonstrate reduced steady-state error, improved disturbance rejection, and transient response. Results confirm a reduction in cycle-to-cycle and cylinder-to-cylinder variations, with a 25% to 75% decrease in the 95% confidence interval for controlled parameters. On-line adaptation ensures robustness against model uncertainties and fuel types.

A linearized version of this optimal law is implemented as a linear controller to adjust the main SOI and duration for MRE. The controller was tested on a Scania D13 Diesel engine using an FPGA implementation. Results indicate that main SOI control improves indicated efficiency, but the linear controller's effectiveness is limited by the system's non-linear behavior, which is fuel-dependent.

entries.title: Stochastic Set-Point Optimization for In-Cycle Closed-Loop Combustion Control Operation
entries.summary: This article investigates the constrained indicated efficiency optimization of set-point references for in-cycle closed-loop combustion regulators. It proposes a novel approach that includes the effect of controlled variables on combustion dispersion, rather than relying on mean-value models, to solve the stochastic optimization problem. A stochastic heat release model is developed and calibrated with data from a Scania D13 engine, using a Monte Carlo approach for simulations. The optimization is constrained by operational limits on maximum pressure, maximum pressure rise rate, and maximum/minimum exhaust temperature. The study demonstrates that by reducing cyclic variations, indicated efficiency can be increased by up to +1.8%unit at low loads and +0.6%unit at medium loads compared to open-loop operation. The greatest benefits are observed when regulating CA50 under demanding maximum pressure rise rate constraints. Considering the risk of pilot misfire can further increase indicated efficiency by +0.3%unit. The benefits of closed-loop combustion control decrease with increasing engine load due to lower sensitivity to combustion variations.

entries.summary: This paper investigates the quantification of FPGA resources for the implementation of closed-loop combustion control algorithms, focusing on in-cycle execution and real-time control of combustion. It details the use of a National Instruments Xilinx Virtex-5 platform for resource quantification and analyzes the requirements for signal processing, including evaluation rate and digital resolution. The study also examines the implementation of in-cylinder pressure signal processing for heat release computation and presents methods to reduce necessary FPGA resources by 80% through optimization of arithmetic and model formulation. The research identifies the number of slices as the main limiting factor for FPGA resources, with a projected need of 18729 slices out of 17280 available. Suggestions for improving these limitations are discussed, providing guidance for selecting FPGAs for in-cycle combustion control alternatives and evaluating the cost-efficiency trade-off.

entries.title: Eﬃciency Optimization by In-Cycle Closed-Loop Combustion Control
entries.summary: This paper is a comprehensive review of in-cycle closed-loop combustion controllers to achieve higher indicated efficiencies. It combines different components of previous investigations by the authors, addressing the validation of on-line estimation methods, in-cycle controllability, and effectiveness of combustion controllers. The work is developed by the combination of simulations and experimental results on a Scania D13 engine. The paper focuses on the design of direct and indirect in-cycle closed-loop combustion controllers with a pilot and main injection to maximize the indicated efficiency under operational and hardware constraints. An in-cycle combustion controller is reviewed for direct efficiency optimization based on an equivalent premixed cycle. By feedback from a virtual pilot mass sensor with a real-time accuracy of ±0.5mg/st, the controller is able to increase the indicated efficiency by +0.42% unit compared to open-loop operation. The effectiveness of the controller is limited due to implementation restrictions and system non-linearities. These are overcome by the indirect controller design. A predictive controller can reduce the cyclic variance of pilot SOC to ±0.4CAD, pilot burnt mass to ±0.6mg, main SOC to ±0.3CAD, and IMEP to ±0.2bar. Accurate predictions are possible by on-line model adaptation. Furthermore, the controller can compensate for pilot misfire to reduce its effect on the CA50 shift from +2.6CAD to +0.5CAD. The reduced dispersion is included in a stochastic combustion model, where Monte Carlo simulations are used to optimize the set-point reference. The results indicate that the efficiency can be increased by +0.6% unit under maximum pressure, maximum pressure rise rate, maximum and minimum exhaust temperature. Despite the controller effectiveness was quantified experimentally, the simulation results must be validated experimentally as well.
